title: Caleb Lomu is learning more than just right tackle at his first training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Caleb Lomu, a 21-year-old rookie for the Patriots, is training primarily at right tackle during his first NFL camp.
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel is testing Lomu's versatility, having him practice at multiple positions including guard and jumbo tight end.
Lomu, a first-round pick, previously played left tackle at Utah and is adjusting to the faster NFL game pace.

title: Kayshon Boutte addresses trade rumors, future with Patriots
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Kayshon Boutte addresses trade rumors, focusing on current play rather than potential moves from the New England Patriots.
Coach Mike Vrabel open to trading a receiver due to crowded wide receiver roster, highlighting Boutte's potential role.
Boutte aims to stay professional and productive in training camp, emphasizing a focus on another successful season.

title: Man charged after allegedly shoving 69-year-old woman at Nantucket ICE protest
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Lee M. Kennedy, 62, charged with assault and disorderly conduct for allegedly pushing a woman at Nantucket ICE protest.
The 69-year-old victim was shoved to the ground during the Indivisible Nantucket march, requiring medical attention.
Kennedy's arraignment is scheduled for September 8; he admitted to pushing the woman amid heavy traffic at the protest.

title: Critical Mass Boston to hold 15-mile bike ride in remembrance of cyclist struck and killed earlier this month
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Critical Mass Boston is organizing a 15-mile bike ride to commemorate cyclist Louisa Gag, struck and killed in Mission Hill.
The remembrance ride starts at Copley Square, promoting bike safety and increased support for the Streets Cabinet.
Participants can use free Bluebikes day passes, highlighting Gag's efforts in expanding the city's bike-share program.

title: This iconic 150-year-old tree was coming down in Belmont. These birds said, not so fast.
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 150-year-old copper beech tree in Belmont was scheduled for removal due to beech leaf disease.
Tree removal was delayed after discovering a nest with American robin nestlings, a federally protected species.
Residents have additional time to visit the tree, with plans to use its wood for community projects after removal.

title: A.J. Brown finally gets going, and other takeaways from Day 5 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: A.J. Brown and quarterback Drake Maye showed improved chemistry in the Patriots' first padded practice of training camp.
Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez was a full participant despite ongoing contract negotiations, engaging actively in 1-on-1 drills.
DeAndre Hopkins ended his brief coaching stint with the Patriots, deciding not to retire from playing in the NFL just yet.

title: Child on bike injured in crash with SUV in Wellesley
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Child on bike sustained potentially serious injuries in collision with SUV in Wellesley at Oakland Street and Woodlawn Avenue.
The incident occurred around 8:51 a.m. and the child was transported to a Boston hospital for evaluation.
SUV driver remained on scene; Wellesley Police are investigating the crash and temporarily closed Oakland Street.

title: Where to go in New England this August
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: The Milford Oyster Festival in Connecticut will occur August 14-15, featuring music, food, and local oysters.
The Foreside Inn, a new boutique hotel in Kittery, Maine, offers access to shops and restaurants in Maine's oldest downtown.
Dine Out Boston runs August 1-15, offering multi-course meals at various price points, including three Saturdays for the first time.

title: Investigation underway after 2 found dead along same stretch of Mass. river
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Two bodies found days apart along the Connecticut River in Western Massachusetts, less than a mile apart.
Hermes Mariano Almonte, 21, drowned near Rock Dam in Turners Falls, no foul play suspected, investigation ongoing.
Another unidentified man's body found near Smead Island; Massachusetts State Police and Montague Police investigating.

title: Federal investigation finds Burlington schools violated the law over ‘graphic’ student survey
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Burlington Public Schools violated federal law by mandating a student survey with sensitive sexual questions, against parental wishes.
The district administered the 2025 Youth Risk Behavior Survey despite parents opting out, and will apologize to affected families.
Burlington must update policies to comply with parental rights laws, and submit future sensitive surveys to the Department of Education.
